# Assumptions Table — Complaint Triage Cost Model

Author: Ugo Ahukannah
Capstone Round 1 · Companion to `cost_analysis.md`

**Generated by `cost_model.py`. Do not hand-edit.** Every figure in the cost analysis
derives from a row below, so an assumption cannot say one thing here and another there.

Each row is classified. **sourced** means a published external figure. **measured**
means measured on this project. **assumption** means a stated property of the client
scenario. **judgement** means my estimate with no citation — these are the soft numbers
and the ones to challenge first.

GBP converted to EUR at 1.17, a judgement, stated rather than hidden.

## The four that move the answer most

| Input | Why it dominates |
|---|---|
| `ca_complaints_per_1000_half` | Drives total volume, and every euro figure scales off it |
| `triage_minutes_assisted` | The softest number here. At 1 minute saved rather than 3, the labour saving falls to about a third |
| `review_days_per_quarter` | 76% of the running cost. Cutting oversight is the only way to make this cheap, and it is the wrong saving |
| `ombudsman_case_fee_gbp` | The entire ROI case rests on avoided escalations, priced at this figure |
